Baseball Betting Tips: Leagues and Events We Cover

OLBG's tipsters share baseball betting tips and predictions across Major League Baseball (MLB), Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB) in Japan and the KBO League in South Korea. We also cover the international World Baseball Classic whenever the tournament is played.

Baseball is one of the four major US team sports, and MLB is split into the National League and the American League. Each MLB team plays 162 regular-season games, so you can expect MLB picks on most days during the season.

How to Place Bets on Our Baseball Tips

Next to each baseball tip above, you will see an 'Add' button. Tap 'Add' on the baseball predictions you want to bet on, and your selections will go straight into your OLBG betslip.

You can add selections one at a time for single bets, or keep adding baseball picks and MLB predictions to build accumulators and permutation bets.

Click an event name to open the event page. There you can see all three baseball markets we cover (Money Line, Game Totals and Run Line), along with how many predictions each outcome has received from our tipsters.

If you are new to baseball betting, our guide to the top baseball betting sites in the UK compares bookmakers and their new customer offers, which will help you choose where to place your baseball bets.

When you are happy with your betslip, compare the odds from different bookmakers at the top of the screen. Select your preferred bookmaker, and you will be taken to their site with your selections already added, ready to place your bet.

You must be 18 or over to bet. Only stake what you can afford to lose, and if gambling is causing you concern, free support is available from GamCare and GambleAware.

Baseball tips on this page cover three markets for individual games: Money Line, Run Line and Game Totals. These are the same across MLB, NPB, KBO and World Baseball Classic games, so once you know them, you can follow our baseball predictions. We also offer ante-post tips on the winner of a league or tournament.

MarketWhat you are predictingWhat decides the bet
Money LineWhich team wins the gameThe final result
Run LineWhich team wins once a run handicap is appliedThe winning margin
Game TotalsWhether the combined runs will be over or under a set numberThe total runs scored by both teams
Ante-postWhich team wins a league or tournamentThe outcome of the competition

Money Line

The Money Line is the simplest baseball market: you pick the team you think will win. The margin does not matter, only the result. Because the favourite's odds are usually short, many bettors turn to the other markets or combine Money Line selections in accumulators.

Run Line

The Run Line is baseball's version of a handicap bet. The favourite is usually given a 1.5-run disadvantage and the underdog a 1.5-run head start. A favourite must therefore win by two runs or more for a Run Line bet on them to win, while a bet on the underdog wins if they win the game or lose by just one run. As baseball games are often decided by a single run, this market can offer very different odds from the Money Line on the same team.

Game Totals

Game Totals is an over/under market on the total runs scored by both teams. The bookmaker sets a line, for example, 8.5 runs, and you decide whether the game will produce more or fewer. The starting pitchers, the ballpark and the weather all influence the total, which is why the pitching stats covered further down this page are so useful for this market.

Extra innings and ties

Extra innings are usually included when bets are settled, so a game that goes beyond nine innings still counts in full. Rules differ by bookmaker, and in NPB and KBO regular-season games can end level after a set number of extra innings, so check how your bookmaker treats a tie before you bet.

Ante-post tips

An ante-post tip is a prediction on who will win a league or tournament, made before the competition is over rather than on a single game. The bet settles when the winner is decided, which can be weeks or months after you place it, so your stake is tied up for longer than it would be on a game bet. Terms vary by bookmaker, so check the rules before you bet.

Bookmakers offer other baseball markets, such as player props, that do not carry OLBG tips. Our complete baseball betting guide covers the main bet types.
Action vs Listed Bets in Baseball Betting

Baseball bets are often tied to the starting pitchers, so many bookmakers let you choose between an action bet and a listed bet on the Money Line, Run Line and Game Totals markets. The rules vary by bookmaker, so check their terms before you bet.

Action bets

If you take an action bet, your bet stands whoever starts the game. Starting pitchers are sometimes changed late, for example because of injury or illness, and an action bet stays in play when that happens. The odds you took are not affected, but they may differ from the listed price, so it is worth comparing both.

Listed bets

If you take a listed bet and either of the named starting pitchers changes, your bet is void, and your stake is returned. This protects you if, for example, you back a team because of a top starter and he is replaced by a lesser pitcher at the last minute.

Bet typeIf a starting pitcher changes
ActionYour bet stands
ListedYour bet is void, and your stake is returned

How Often Do Baseball Favourites Win in the MLB, NPB and KBO?

These are the three professional baseball leagues we cover tips for during the regular season: MLB in the USA, NPB in Japan and the KBO in South Korea. The table shows how often the favourite has won at home and on the road over the last five completed seasons.

MLB favourites have the highest win rate in both home and road games, while NPB favourites have the lowest. Favourites win more often at home than on the road in all three leagues, with the smallest difference in the KBO.

A high win rate does not make a favourite good value, as the price you take matters as much as how often they win.

Key Baseball Stats and Factors to Consider Before Betting

Baseball is decided by runs scored and runs prevented, so team and pitcher stats, along with the ballpark and weather, are worth a look before you choose your baseball picks. As the starting pitcher has such a big influence on each game, the pitching stats below are especially useful.

StatWhat it measuresRough guide
ERA (Earned Run Average)The number of earned runs a pitcher allows per nine inningsLower is better. Under 4.00 is generally considered good, and under 3.00 excellent
WHIP (Walks and Hits per Inning Pitched)How many runners a pitcher allows on base each inning through walks and hitsLower is better. Around 1.20 is generally considered good, which works out at almost 11 baserunners per nine innings
Quality startsGames where the starting pitcher lasts at least six innings and allows no more than three earned runsA high percentage of quality starts points to a reliable starter
OBP (On-Base Percentage)How often a hitter or team reaches base through a hit, a walk or a hit by pitchHigher is better. Around .325 is generally considered a good team figure

These benchmarks are rough guides, as league-wide averages change from season to season and differ between MLB, NPB and KBO.

Ballpark, Weather and Travel

Context can matter as much as a pitcher's numbers, especially for Game Totals. The table below shows what to check before you back a pick.

FactorWhat to checkWhy it matters
BallparkPark factor, which compares runs scored at a ground with the league average, and outfield dimensionsSome parks favour hitters and others favour pitchers, which affects the total
WeatherWind speed and direction, and temperatureWind blowing out and warm air can help the ball carry, while wind blowing in and cold air can hold it up. Roofed stadiums are less affected
Rest and travelConsecutive games, long trips and cross-time-zone travelTired teams and heavily used bullpens can perform below their usual level
